previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic heart failure, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted with fever, cough, and hypoxia. He was transferred from a rehab facility where he had been recovering from a prior admission for hip pain. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis, elevated BNP, and chest imaging showing pulmonary edema and worsening opacities concerning for healthcare-associated pneumonia. He was treated with vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to ceftazidime for dialysis compatibility. His infection markers improved, oxygen was weaned off, and he was stabilized on his baseline heart failure and diabetes regimens. Cinacalcet was held due to low calcium. A stage II coccygeal pressure ulcer was monitored without intervention. He completed a dialysis session prior to discharge and was transitioned back to extended care with plans to complete a seven-day antibiotic course. He was alert, ambulatory with assistance, and clinically improved at discharge.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Non-functioning left upper extremity AV fistula.

FINDINGS:  Duplex and color Doppler of the left upper extremity was performed.
There is patency of the arterial-venous anastomosis in this patient with a
left upper extremity AV fistula.  However, the native draining vein shows
non-occlusive thrombus.  More centrally, there appears to be an intervening
graft joining the draining vein.  This shows complete thrombosis throughout
its course up to its confluence with the axillary vein.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Patent brachial artery and arterial-venous anastomosis.
2.  Thrombosis of the draining vein with partial occlusion more proximal and
complete occlusion more centrally.

INDICATION:  ___ man with end-stage renal disease.  Left
brachiocephalic fistula placed in ___.  Interposition graft placed in ___
from the mid fistula to the left axillary vein.  Presents with recent dialysis
access thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  No prior thrombolysis at this institution

TECHNIQUE  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ resident), Dr. ___
___ radiology attending) and, subsequently, Dr. ___
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure.  The attendings,
Drs.   ___ were present and supervising throughout the
procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Mild sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
175mcg of fentanyl and 0 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 3 hr and 45 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, 5000 units IV heparin, 10 mg t-PA

CONTRAST: 126 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  45 min, 29 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Left upper extremity AV fistula and graft fistulogram.

2. Axillary, subclavian and super vena cava venography.

3. Chemical and mechanical thrombolysis of the thrombosed graft and outflow
vein using the Angiojet and Cleaner devices.

4. Balloon angioplasty of the intragraft, outflow vein and inflow artery
stenoses.

5.  ___ balloon pull through of the arterial inflow and graft.

 PROCEDURE DETAILS: After explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives to
the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The
patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
exam table. The patient, procedure, and site were confirmed during a
pre-procedure time-out performed per ___ protocol. The left upper extremity
was prepped, stabilized, and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Clinical examination demonstrated a palpable, but completely thrombosed
fistula and graft in the left upper extremity. Further evaluation by targeted
ultrasound demonstrated a completely thrombosed graft extending into the
outflow vein.

Following administration of subcutaneous lidocaine, antegrade (directed
towards the venous outflow) access into the thrombosed fistula was obtained
under continuous ultrasound guidance using a 21G micropuncture needle.
Permanent ultrasound images were saved. An 0.018 wire was then advanced into
the outflow vein under fluoroscopic guidance. A 4.5F micropuncture sheath was
advanced and used to exchange for an 0.035 Glidewire. The glide wire was
advance to the level of the subclavian vein. A short 6 ___ sheath was
placed over the wire. A ___ Kumpe catheter was then advanced over the wire and
slowly withdrawn while injecting dilute contrast to establish the distal
extent of thrombus into the outflow vein.

Retrograde access to the interposition graft directed towards the arterial
inflow was then obtained in a similar fashion using continuous ultrasound and
intermittent fluoroscopic guidance. Permanent ultrasound images were saved.
Care was taken not to advance the wire into the inflow brachial artery prior
to thrombolysis.  At this point 4000 IU of heparin was administered
systemically.

Tissue plasminogen activator was administered along the entire length of the
thrombosed graft and outflow vein using the AngioJet pulse spray device in the
both antegrade and retrograde directions. A total of 10 mg was infused. The
tPA was allowed to dwell for approximately 10 minutes. The AngioJet device was
then switched to thrombectomy mode and mechanical thrombectomy was performed
from the antegrade and retrograde approaches. An 0.035 glidewire was directed
into the inflow brachial artery and advanced proximally. A 5.5 ___ ___
balloon was advanced beyond the arterial anastomosis, partially inflated and
pullback was performed through the arterial anastomosis and through graft.

Subsequently, angioplasty was performed along the length of the graft and
outflow vein using a 6 x 40 mm balloon.  Fistulogram confirmed presence of
residual clot in the fistula and graft. An additional 1000 units of IV heparin
was administered. Repeat mechanical thrombectomy with the Angiojet device jet
device was performed. Balloon angioplasty was performed along the length of
the fistula, graft, and outflow using a 7 x 40 mm balloon. A Cleaner XT device
was used to mechanically clear retained thrombus. Repeat balloon angioplasty
was performed with an 8 x 40 mm balloon. The fistulogram now showed good
patency of the fistula, graft, and venous outflow.

A stricture at the arterial anastomosis was serially dilated with a 6 x 40 mm
and 7 x 40 mm balloons. A completion fistulogram was performed from the
proximal brachial artery demonstrating brisk flow throughout the entire graft
with no residual stenosis. Clinical examination revealed a satisfactory thrill
along the length of the graft. The sheaths were removed and hemostasis was
achieved with two ___ purse string sutures.

During the course of thrombectomy, the patient became transiently hypoxic with
oxygen saturations in the high ___. Simultaneously, the patient complained of
mild chest pain. In the setting of thrombectomy of a large thrombus burden,
the symptoms were attributed to a small pulmonary embolism. The patient was
placed on a non-rebreather mask. At the conclusion of the procedure, the
patient's oxygen saturation was 100% and he was free of chest pain.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Extensive thrombosis of the left upper extremity AV fistula and
interposition graft to the level of the outflow vein.

2. Outflow vein stenosis with improvement following angioplasty to 8 mm.

3. Inflow artery stenosis with improvement following angioplasty to 7 mm.

IMPRESSION: 

Satisfactory restoration of flow within the left upper extremity fistula and
graft following chemical and mechanical thrombolysis with a good angiographic
and clinical result.

 The findings and complications were discussed by Dr. ___ with
sub-intern ___  on the telephone on ___ at 14:20.
